title: Health signal aggregation — lab notes & scoring logic
content:
Purpose
Quick research / working notes for a more formalized customer health aggregation model. This doc is intentionally informal — experiments, heuristics, and open questions are captured here. Goal: propose an actionable scoring formula that maps observable signals to renewal risk tiers and triage actions for CSMs and AEs.

Background / motivation
- Current CS scoring is a brittle mix of spreadsheets and per-CSM heuristics. We need a repeatable logic that: 1) surfaces high-risk accounts early, 2) prioritizes outreach with clear playbook steps, 3) is explainable during QBRs and renewal conversations.
- Constraints: limited instrumentation in some customers (on-prem), latency of some signals (billing appears weekly), and tradeoffs between precision and noise.

Signal inventory (raw sources & cadence)
- Usage: daily tokens/day, weekly request counts (hosted API). (source: telemetry API)
- Active users: distinct engineers hitting endpoints (weekly active devs).
- Feature adoption: callouts to new features (streaming, reranking) — binary per feature per account (monthly).
- Error surface: 5xx rate, request timeouts (daily).
- Latency SLA breaches: % requests > target ms (daily/weekly).
- Support volume: tickets opened / week, escalations (ticketing system).
- NPS/CSAT snippets: ad hoc notes from CSMs (quarterly).
- Billing anomalies: unexpected spend drop or spike (monthly or on-reporting).
- Health checks: scheduled sync success rate (for private/on-prem) (daily/weekly).

Pre-processing rules (notes)
- Smooth noisy signals with short EWMA (alpha = 0.25) over 7-day window for usage and errors.
- For accounts with sparse telemetry (e.g., on-prem with logging lag), fallback to support tickets + CSM notes as primary signals.
- Normalize signals to 0–100 by mapping historical 1st–99th percentiles to range; cap outliers.

Signal categories and rationale
- Adoption (40% total weight): tokens/day trend (20%), active devs (10%), feature adoption breadth (10%). Rationale: adoption is the strongest predictor of expansion and renewal.
- Reliability (25%): 5xx rate (10%), SLA breaches (10%), sync failure rate (5%). Reliability degradation often triggers churn or escalations.
- Engagement (15%): support volume (5%), CS touch frequency (5%), product feedback / PRs (5%). Engagement speaks to health but sometimes noisy.
- Economic signals (10%): billing anomalies (10%). Sudden cost drops + no engagement = risk.
- Qualitative (10%): NPS/CSAT and CSM subjective risk note (10%). Never solely relied on but useful as tie-breaker.

Proposed scoring formula (high level)
1) Compute normalized signal value S_i in [0,100] for each atomic signal i. Higher = healthier. For negative signals (errors, SLA breaches), invert so higher means better.
2) Aggregate weighted category scores: CategoryScore_c = sum_i (w_i * S_i) / sum(w_i)  -> result 0–100 per category.
3) Overall Health = sum_c (W_c * CategoryScore_c) / sum(W_c). Weights W_c per categories above (Adoption 40, Reliability 25, Engagement 15, Economic 10, Qual 10).
4) Map Overall Health to tiers: Green >= 75, Yellow 50–74, Red < 50. These were chosen to bias earlier detection (i.e., conservative).

Example / toy calculations (three accounts)
- Account A (growing): tokens/day norm 85, active devs 90, feature breadth 70 => adoption cat ~82. Reliability cat 95, Engagement 70, Economic 90, Qual 85 -> overall ~86 -> Green.
- Account B (stagnant but reliable): adoption 45, reliability 90, engagement 40, econ 60, qual 50 -> overall ~59 -> Yellow (needs playbook).
- Account C (high errors): adoption 60, reliability 25 (errors + SLA breaches), engagement 30, econ 40, qual 35 -> overall ~38 -> Red (immediate action).

Risk flags (automated triggers separate from tier)
- Critical risk (raise to AE + SRE): any single-day 5xx rate spike > 3x baseline AND >1% absolute error rate.
- Contracted SLA miss: 3 consecutive days with >5% latency SLA breach -> auto-incident + customer alert.
- Usage drop: >40% M/M drop in tokens and no planned reason (e.g., known cutoff) -> schedule renewal health check.
- Quiet account: <3 API calls/week for 30 days after initial onboarding completion -> schedule "lost engagement" play.

Triage playbooks (quick bullets)
- Green (no proactive outreach required): include positive signal highlights in QBR, flag for potential expansion leads.
- Yellow (early intervention): CSM re-education session on top features, run a 30-day success plan with defined adoption milestones. If adoption stagnates after 30 days, escalate to AE for commercial check-in.
- Red (urgent): Immediate incident review with SRE (if reliability), 48-hour remediation plan, daily standups with customer until stable. For adoption-led reds, quick audit of onboarding, shadow calls, and scope mini-PoC to regain confidence.

CSM playbook checklist (to automate in ticket)
- Attach last 90-day usage chart + top failing endpoints.
- List last three CSM touches and topics.
- Recommended 3 action steps (technical, adoption, commercial).
- Owner assigned + due date (default 7 days for Yellow, 48 hours for Red).

QBR snippets (what to include)
- Slide: Health snapshot (Overall score + category bars) with trend over last 90 days.
- Slide: Top 3 wins + Top 3 risks (tied to signals).
- Handout: Action plan with owners and dates (exported from CS tooling).

Open questions / heuristics to validate
- Weight sensitivity: how sensitive are renewals to adoption weight vs reliability weight? Quick experiment: hold reliability constant, vary adoption weight ±10 and measure historical recall/precision on churn 6–12 months out.
- Threshold calibration: are Green/Yellow/Red cutoffs optimal? Run retrospective on last 24 renewals to see distribution and pick cutoffs that maximize early recall with acceptable false positives (target false positive rate <20%).
- Signal gaps for on-prem: how much do we lose when telemetry is delayed? Need to test model performance on subset of private deployments.

Instrumentation & product asks (engineering tickets)
- Add daily token count and distinct active devs per account to telemetry export. (JIRA-4019)
- Include per-feature usage flags for new capabilities (streaming, reranking). (JIRA-4021)
- Expose rolling 7-day 95th percentile latency metric to CS dashboard (PR in cs-tools). (GH-89)

Operational notes / implementation plan (MVP)
- MVP scope: implement aggregation logic in CS analytics job, populate dashboard and generate weekly "Top 50 At-Risk" list. Timebox: 6 weeks.
- Iteration 1: tune weights with historical backtest, add automated risk flags. (3 weeks)
- Iteration 2: connect playbook automation to ticketing system (auto-create play tasks when Yellow/Red). (2 weeks)

Owner & next steps
- Owner: Hannah Li (CS Lead for risk signals) — build MVP spec and coordinate PRs.
- Next steps this sprint: finalize normalization buckets (due 2025-02-05), run 6-month retrospective test (due 2025-02-16), open engineering tickets (done), prototype dashboard JSON (due 2025-02-24).

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep qualitative signal weight low but never drop it; CSM notes often explain anomalies.
- Watch for correlation between feature breadth and expansion velocity — may want to add sigmoid transform for adoption signals to capture step-changes.
- Be conservative on thresholds; CSM workload is limited — prefer fewer but higher-precision alerts.

References & links
- Confluence: health-score-overview (linked above).
- JIRA: JIRA-3492 (backtest task), JIRA-4019 (telemetry), JIRA-4021 (feature flags).
- GitHub: cs-tools PR 87 — initial dashboard schema.

If you want to iterate on the sample weights or run a backtest on a particular cohort (e.g., SMB vs enterprise), add a note here and I will attach the cohort export and results.

-- end of lab notes --
